title: L2 RX packet processing on system workqueue can starve all other system work
description: Found by security+robustness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-sb0b (P2). rx_work_fn on the cooperative system workqueue runs the full lichen_l2_input chain: rx_mutex K_FOREVER, Schnorr-48 verify (CPU-bound, up to N peers per attacker frame), SCHC decompress, and net_pkt_rx_alloc_with_buffer with CONFIG_LICHEN_L2_RX_ALLOC_TIMEOUT_MS (default 50ms) - all unpreeemptible at cooperative priority, shared with USB/udc work, net DAD/ND delayed work, mgmt events. A radio-range attacker (~40fps at SF7) can hold sysworkq near-permanently. Mitigations to evaluate: dedicated RX workqueue (k_work_queue_start, prio like old RX_THREAD_PRIORITY), shrinking the alloc timeout for sysworkq builds, or moving net_pkt alloc off the hot path. Stack budgets were migrated in sb0b (puck 8192, gateway boards 12288, nucleo_wl55jc 2048 = old RX default); budget parity is verified, sharing is the issue.
